transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel, Diego Marquez (Redwood); Ava Lin, Marcus Cho, Priya Nair, Ethan Ross (Elm)

Summary (auto): Elm is evaluating consolidation from a mix of OpenAI/Anthropic + an internal vLLM/TGI cluster. They need eval parity, predictable tail latency, and org-level compliance (SOC2, SSO). They want a small sprint/POC to validate output parity and five-day pilot options for Dedicated or Private deployments.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm samira from redwood inference — i'm the AE on this account and with me is diego our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Ava: hey, good thanks. excited to dig in. quick note, we are on slightly tight timeline, aiming to pick a direction by end of q2.
[00:12] Samira: great that's helpful. diego will run most of the tech bits, i'll cover commercial and security follow ups. can we go around and do a 30-second intros?
[00:19] Ava: ava lin, head of ml, overseeing model infra and cross-team evaluation.
[00:23] Marcus: marcus cho, infra lead, owns our on-prem cluster and networking.
[00:26] Priya: priya nair, security and compliance, mainly SOC2 and data residency.
[00:30] Ethan: ethan ross, product, focused on latency/SLOs for user-facing features.
[00:34] Diego: diego marquez, se, I'll be doing the bench and integration plan.

[00:45] Samira: cool. ava, can you give a quick picture of your current stack and what you mean by consolidation?
[00:50] Ava: yeah. right now we split workloads — high-risk PII workflows run through our on-prem vLLM instances using TGI and some custom kernels, lower-sensitivity generation uses OpenAI and Anthropic via their hosted apis. we've seen cost creep and variance in latency, also templatized prompt outputs don't always match between vendors.
[01:07] Samira: totally. and the parity ask is — you want Redwood to match the OpenAI/Anthropic outputs exactly or just within an acceptable delta for your eval metrics?
[01:14] Ava: acceptable delta. our eval suite is BLEU/ROUGE-ish but also human-annotated F1 for hallucination and instruction-following. if redwood can get us within the same distribution and not regress on hallucination by more than 5%, that's good.
[01:28] Ethan: and for product we're mostly worried about 95th percentile latency under load, that has to stay under 350ms for short chat features.

[01:38] Diego: okay, that's useful. quick clarifying q: when you mention vLLM/TGI on-prem, are you managing your own KV cache and shards? is there a custom attention kernel?
[01:46] Marcus: for the most part yes — we run vllm with some patched kernels, we also cache commonly used prefixes in redis, plus a local kv-layer. it's pretty tuned.
[01:54] Diego: good to know, because when we talk about prefix/KV caching differences we want to align runtimes. redwood's runtime does continuous batching and KV cache hotwarm strategies but naming may be off in transcripts — it's K-V cash sometimes — sorry, internal joke.
[02:08] Priya: on security, we need to know how key management works. our legal reqs: customer-managed keys (KMS/hsm), SSO via saml, audit logs for every inference request for 90 days, and data residency in eu for eu customers. can redwood private satisfy that?
[02:23] Samira: yes, private deployments support customer KMS integrations and audit log exports. we have an enterprise package for the retention windows. for hosted we also offer encrypted-at-rest keys, but private gives you full control. we'll share our compliance pack.
[02:35] Diego: and just to add, our dedicated clusters can live in region and be isolated — that's between hosted and private in terms of control/effort.

[02:46] Ava: cost question — we currently pay vendor X for hosted usage and then ops for the on-prem cluster. how do dedicated commitments compare?
[02:53] Samira: overview: hosted is usage-based (per-token), low friction. dedicated is reserved capacity monthly with a baseline commit and burst options; it's more predictable cost-per-token. private has platform licensing and infra ops. we'll send a matrix with numbers — diego can also share expected throughput per GPU type.

[03:10] Ethan: about model variants — we run a mix of Llama2 derivatives and some Claude-like models. do you host open models or is there model conversion required?
[03:19] Diego: we run open model catalog plus supported conversions. sometimes tokenizer differences or small architecture variants cause subtle output drift. part of the POC is getting prompt/adapter parity and measuring deltas. we typically do a small model pin — run the same weights or a verified variant.

[03:33] Marcus: our infra team is worried about deployment surface area. how much change to networking and firewall rules for private? we need an estimate of ports and egress.
[03:41] Diego: Private deploy needs a control-plane handshake, outbound-to-redwood-control only on specific ports, or in full airgapped mode we can do offline bundles. we'll send a network runbook.

[03:52] Priya: auditing: can you give examples of request-level logs? i want to know what fields are captured, are prompts stored, how to redact?
[03:58] Samira: yes, we capture request id, model, token counts, latency, route decisions, and an optional payload log. for regulated workflows you can opt out of storing raw prompts; we can provide hashed pseudonymized request bodies.

[04:12] Ava: ok good. what's your suggested POC?
[04:15] Diego: propose a two-phase sprint: phase 1 — parity bench: we run Elm's 2000-prompt eval set across current baselines (OpenAI + Anthropic + vLLM local) and Redwood's hosted and dedicated config to measure output delta, latency distribution, and token cost. phase 2 — integration pilot: a small routing test (5k requests/day) on dedicated or private with KV cache warmup.
[04:37] Ethan: timeline?
[04:38] Diego: phase 1 could be run in 48-72 hours once we get the prompt set and credentials for the hosted vendors. phase 2 is 2-3 weeks for a minimal pilot.
[04:47] Ava: that fits our q2 decision window. are there known gotchas when porting from TGI and vLLM?
[04:53] Diego: tokenizer mismatches, slight differences in sampling seeds and math kernels, and caching semantics. also TGI's beam search defaults, if you're using nonstandard decoding, that can change outputs. we normally add a normalization layer — small prompt wrappers — to get better parity.
[05:08] Marcus: any perf loss moving from our patched kernels to redwood runtime? we rely on nvfuser-like kernels for some ops.
[05:14] Diego: our runtime selects kernels per model and length distribution; in some rare cases micro-ops differ — but we can run microbenchmarks on your patched models. if you need exact same kernel stack we can also support a private deploy that runs your binaries, though that's more complex.
[05:30] Priya: contract/legal — do you do data processing agreements that list roles and subprocessor disclosures?
[05:35] Samira: yes, DPA and subprocessor list available. we'll include that in the security pack.

[05:43] Ethan: about routing — can we do latency-first for interactive users and cost-first for batch?
[05:49] Diego: yep, smart routing policies exist — you can set route by latency SLO, cost budget, or region; fallback models are supported automatically when capacity bumps happen.

[05:58] Ava: for eval metrics, we will need human annotation for hallucination, not just automated metrics. can redwood help with instrumentation to capture those examples?
[06:06] Diego: we can export candidate outputs and link them to request ids which your annotation tool can ingest. we also have lightweight sampling hooks you can drop into prod to capture rare failure modes.

[06:18] Priya: slightly concerned about vendor lock-in, if we bake tooling into redwood routing and cache, what is exit-path look like?
[06:25] Samira: exit-path is a standard ask — we provide export tools for KV caches, model pin configs, routing rules and prompt sets. plus we can map equivalence to vLLM/TGI configs to make a reverse migration easier.

[06:37] Ethan: what's next on scheduling?
[06:39] Samira: action items — diego will get the bench script prepared, samira will share pricing + security docs. we'll plan the parity bench for next week if elm can send the prompt pack and vendor keys.

[06:49] Ava: i'll coordinate prompt pack and annotation access. expect an email with data pointers by feb 10.
[06:54] Marcus: i'll review the network runbook once you send it.

[07:00] Samira: awesome. any final q's?
[07:02] Priya: one small thing — do you have references for customers who did private deploy with HSM?
[07:07] Samira: yes, we can share two redacted case studies. i'll include in the security pack.

[07:13] Diego: last technical note — when you send the prompt pack, include examples of your warm prefixes and any custom tokenizer files, that saves time.
[07:21] Ava: will do. thanks everyone.

[07:25] Samira: thanks all. we'll follow up with the timeline and next steps.

- Diego to run parity benchmark and share results (due 2027-02-12).
